From today, Runna subscribers can use the brand new "Adapt for Heat" feature, which automatically adjusts pace targets based on local temperature and humidity. Details are as follows.

Runna adds training tools for high temperatures

Personalised running coach app Runna announced today (the 17th) three updates covering the entire training cycle — from training in hot weather to post-race recovery.

The brand new "Adapt for Heat" feature launches today, helping users find cooler running windows and suggesting adjusted pace targets based on feels-like temperature, training duration, and specific workouts.

The "Adapt for Heat" feature displays colour-coded hourly weather forecasts, allowing users to see at a glance the best times to run and plan accordingly.

The following is Runna's introduction to this new feature:

Runna also announced the relaunch of the "Post-Race Recovery Plan" feature. When users open any race plan from 5K to 50K, the system automatically generates a corresponding training programme. Runna head coach and former Olympian Steph Kessell said these plans are designed by professional coaches to help runners "reduce the risk of overtraining or injury".

Finally, the platform also announced a new feature, "Upcoming Plans", set to launch in August. This feature lets users pre-schedule multiple training plans and seamlessly transition from one to the next after completing the previous one, further simplifying long-term training arrangements.

The following is Runna's introduction to the benefits of the "Upcoming Plans" feature:

Plan a full year of training in just minutes: runners can overlay races, phased goals, and training cycles for a clear view of the entire year's training at a glance.
